circuit_character: Undulating circuit where rhythm and flow are important
Few overtaking opportunities so qualifying position is critical
The GP loop is where a lot of time can be found
Confidence is required through the GP loop
build_lap_notes: Manage the gap on build laps

notes: Track limit sensors are on the exit of T2 and T3

T1.name: Paddock Hill
driving_focus: Bring the car over to the left across the start-finish line
Point straight at the marshals' post
Getting the car straight for braking is more important than being on the white line
Wait until over the crest before braking
Drop the brake and turn in at the access road on the left
Be back to full throttle by the apex
You can run two wheels on the exit kerb
Do not put the whole car on the exit kerb or it will bottom out and lose speed
Get the rotation done before the apex
Have confidence that the compression will support you

common_errors: Braking before the crest
Not straight enough for braking
Holding the brake too deep and carrying understeer
Not back to full throttle by the apex
Using too much exit kerb and bottoming

T2.name: Druids
driving_focus: Brake hard in a straight line before the bridge point
Do not use the apex kerb
You can vee the corner a little but keep the car within about 1m of the kerb
Be patient getting back to power
Focus on good rotation to straighten the car
Use the road to the white line on exit
Keep pulling right on exit to prepare for turn 3
Be very direct with the corner
Focus on braking with a flat car
Have a good bleed off

common_errors: Picking up throttle too early and creating understeer or a snap
Poor rotation leaving the car crooked on exit
Using the apex kerb
Not getting the car flat for braking

T3.name: Graham Hill
driving_focus: Get the car straight for braking and take the load out of it
A little entry track extension can be used
Aim to have the middle of the car pointing towards the end of the grandstand
Use a short sharp brake
Release the brake as you turn in
Turn and go
Be on power by the apex kerb
You can use a little apex kerb
You can put a wheel on the exit kerb
Do not run over the exit kerb because there is a track-limits sensor

common_errors: Braking with too much lateral load still in the car
Slow brake release reducing rotation
Late throttle at the apex
Overusing the exit kerb and triggering track limits

T4.name: Graham Hill
driving_focus: Brake at the orange marker just after the backslash board
Start turning in before the end of the kerb
Be patient and do not turn too early
The white line is the apex
Be flat by the apex
Rotate well before the apex and do not scrub speed on exit
You can put a wheel on the exit kerb
Do not run over the exit kerb because there is a track-limits sensor
Time gained here is on exit, not entry

common_errors: Turning too early
Still rotating at the apex
Scrubbing speed on exit
Trying to gain time on entry instead of exit

T5.name: Hawthorns
driving_focus: Turn in then lift with a small brake
Keep the speed up through the corner
Do not turn in too early
Turning too early delays throttle pickup and increases instability
Start progressively squeezing on power before the apex
Avoid touching the inside kerb
You can put a wheel on the exit kerb
Pedal inputs and pitch control are key
The corner is dirty offline so the right line is critical

common_errors: Turning too early
Late throttle pickup
Too much brake or lift costing speed
Touching the inside kerb and unsettling the car
Poor confidence or instability from bad line

T6.name: Westfield
driving_focus: Brake at the orange marker just before the orange part of the Armco
Ensure a flat car while braking
Bleed off nicely and turn in
Get rotated before the apex kerb
Look to get behind the apex kerb
Pick up power to settle the car on exit
Use only the red and white exit kerb
Any more exit kerb risks bottoming out and being unable to get back on track
Quick early rotation is critical
As the track drops away on exit it is even more important to get the rotation done early

common_errors: Braking with the car still loaded
Not rotating early enough
Delayed throttle on exit
Using too much exit kerb and bottoming

T7.name: Westfield
driving_focus: Arrive following the arc of the white line
This allows more controlled turn-in and weight transfer
Brake just before the orange Armco end
Feed in the power before the apex to settle the car
Use the apex kerb
Run out to the white line using all the track
Quick early rotation is critical
As the track drops away on exit it is even more important to get the rotation done early

common_errors: Too abrupt a turn-in from poor approach line
Late rotation
Not feeding power before the apex
Leaving track width unused on exit

T8.name: Sterlings
driving_focus: Work hard to bring the car back over and parallel to the white line ready for braking
Brake just before the orange Armco marker
Start to turn in after the white line which crosses the track
As soon as you are off the brake, feed in the power
Use the dip of the track to help support the car
You can use a little apex kerb
Use all of the exit kerb
A nice controlled bleed of the brake helps the rotation
Before the compression starts you should be feeding in the power
Think exit

common_errors: Poor setup to the white line before braking
Turning in too early
Waiting too long to feed in power
Not using the support from the compression and dip

T9.name: Clearways
driving_focus: Brake at the backslash board with a flat car parallel to the white line
Bleed off the brake and turn in at the start of the tarmac patch on the left
The apex is right at the crest
The apex point is where the inside kerb transitions from thick to thin
Be confident and run close to the white line
Be on the limit and against the kerb
The compression of the corner will help keep the car in
Use the brake release to help rotate before the apex
Apply the power well for a strong exit
Think exit

common_errors: Braking with the car not flat
Turning in too early or too late relative to the tarmac patch
Weak brake release so the car does not rotate before the apex
Not confident enough at the outside white line
Poor power application hurting the exit

notes: The sector map on page 2 shows turns numbered 1 to 9

intended_use: Use as context layer on top of delta analysis
Do not let advisory override measured data
Prefer advisory-based comments when a measured behaviour clearly conflicts with target technique
example_checks: If throttle pickup occurs materially after the stated target point, flag as late throttle relative to the booklet
If gear channel differs from target gear at corner minimum speed, flag gear mismatch
If brake release is prolonged where the booklet asks for short sharp braking or quick rotation, flag weak rotation setup
If exit speed is poor where the booklet repeatedly stresses exit, prioritise the exit-focused comment
